questions.question: The least positive integral value of $\alpha$, for which the angle between the vectors $\alpha \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\alpha \hat{i} + 2\alpha \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$ is acute, is _____.

We know that, $\vec{a}.\vec{b} = \left(\vec{a}\right)\left(\vec{b}\right)\cos \theta \implies \cos \theta = \frac{(\alpha \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) \cdot (\alpha \hat{i} + 2\alpha \hat{j} - 2\hat{k})}{\sqrt{{\alpha }^{2} + 4 + 4}\sqrt{{\alpha }^{2} + 4{\alpha }^{2} + 4}} \implies \cos \theta = \frac{{\alpha }^{2} - 4\alpha - 4}{\sqrt{{\alpha }^{2} + 8}\sqrt{5{\alpha }^{2} + 4}}$

Since $\theta$ is acute,

$\implies {\alpha }^{2} - 4\alpha - 4 > 0 \implies {\alpha }^{2} - 4\alpha + 4 > 8 \implies (\alpha - 2{)}^{2} > 8 \implies \alpha - 2 > 2\sqrt{2}$ or $\alpha - 2 < - 2\sqrt{2} \alpha > 2 + 2\sqrt{2}$ or $\alpha < 2 - 2\sqrt{2}$

questions.question: Let $\vec{a},\vec{b},\vec{c}$ be three vectors such that $\left(\vec{a}\right) = \sqrt{31},4\left(\vec{b}\right) = \left(\vec{c}\right) = 2$ and $2\left(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\right) = 3\left(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}\right)$. If the angle between $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is $\frac{2\pi }{3}$, then ${\left(\frac{\vec{a} \times \vec{c}}{\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}}\right)}^{2}$ is equal to _____ .
questions.explanation:
Given,

$\left(\vec{a}\right) = \sqrt{31},4\left(\vec{b}\right) = \left(\vec{c}\right) = 2$, $2\left(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\right) = 3\left(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}\right)$ and angle between $\vec{b} & \vec{c}$ is given as $\frac{2\pi }{3}$

Now solving, $3\left(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}\right) + 2\left(\vec{b} \times \vec{a}\right) = 0 \implies \left(3\vec{c} \times 2\vec{b}\right) \times \vec{a} = 0$

Means $\left(3\vec{c} \times 2\vec{b}\right) & \vec{a}$ are parallel vector,

So, let $3\vec{c} \times 2\vec{b} = \lambda \vec{a}$

Now squaring both sides we get,

$9{\left(\vec{c}\right)}^{2} + 4{\left(\vec{b}\right)}^{2} + 12\left(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}\right) = {\lambda }^{2}{\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2} \implies 36 + 1 + 12 \times \frac{1}{2} \times 2\left(\cos \left(2\frac{\pi }{3}\right)\right) = {\lambda }^{2}\left(31\right) \implies {\lambda }^{2} = 1 \implies \lambda = \pm 1$

Now putting the value of $\lambda$ in $\left(3\vec{c} \times 2\vec{b}\right) = \lambda \vec{a}$ we get,

$3\vec{c} + 2\vec{b} = \pm \vec{a} \dots \left(1\right)$

Now taking dot product with $\vec{b}$ in above equation we get,

$3\left(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}\right) + 2\left(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{b}\right) = \pm \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} \implies \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = \pm \left( - \frac{3}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\right) = \pm \left( - 1\right) \implies {\left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}\right)}^{2} = 1$

Again taking $3\left(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}\right) = 2\left(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\right)$ and sqauring both side,

$\implies {\left(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}\right)}^{2} = \frac{4}{9}{\left(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\right)}^{2} \implies {\left(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}\right)}^{2} = \frac{4}{9}\left({\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2}{\left(\vec{b}\right)}^{2} - {\left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}\right)}^{2}\right) \implies {\left(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}\right)}^{2} = \frac{4}{9}\left(\frac{31}{4} - \left(1\right)\right) \implies {\left(\vec{c} \times \vec{a}\right)}^{2} = \frac{4}{9} \times \frac{27}{4} = 3$

Hence, the value of ${\left(\frac{\vec{a} \times \vec{c}}{\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}}\right)}^{2} = \frac{3}{1} = 3$.

Given,

Now squaring both side we get,

$\implies {\left(\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\vec{a} + \vec{b} - \vec{c}\right)}^{2} \implies {\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\vec{b}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\vec{c}\right)}^{2} + 2\left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}\right) + 2\left(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}\right) + 2\left(\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}\right) = {\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\vec{b}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\vec{c}\right)}^{2} + 2\left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}\right) - 2\left(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}\right) - 2\left(\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}\right) \implies 2\left(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}\right) + 2\left(\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}\right) = - 2\left(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}\right) + 2\left(\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}\right) \implies 4\left(\left(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c}\right) + \left(\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}\right)\right) = 0$

Now here given $\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} = 0$, so

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} = 0$ which means $\vec{c} & \vec{a}$ are perpendicular vector, so statement $\left(B\right)$ is false,

Now statement$\left(A\right) : \left(\vec{a} + \lambda \vec{c}\right) \ge \left(\vec{a}\right) \implies {\left(\vec{a} + \lambda \vec{c}\right)}^{2} \ge {\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2} \implies {\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2} + \lambda {\left(\vec{c}\right)}^{2} + 2\left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}\right) \ge {\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2} \implies \lambda {\left(\vec{c}\right)}^{2} + 2\left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}\right) \ge 0 \implies \lambda {\left(\vec{c}\right)}^{2} \ge 0$

And $\vec{a} \times (\vec{b} + \vec{c}) = \vec{0}$,

So, $\vec{a} \times \left(\vec{b} + \vec{c}\right) = \vec{0} \implies \vec{a} \times \vec{b} + \vec{a} \times \vec{c} = \vec{0} \implies \vec{a} \times \vec{b} = - \vec{a} \times \vec{c} \implies \vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \vec{c} \times \vec{a} \implies \left( \begin{matrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & - 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{matrix} \right) = \left( \begin{matrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ x & y & z \\ 1 & - 2 & 3\end{matrix} \right) \implies - 5\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k} = \hat{i}\left(3y + 2z\right) + \hat{j}\left(z - 3x\right) + \hat{k}\left( - 2x - y\right)$

On comparing we get,

$3y + 2z = - 5$ .....(i)

$z - 3x = 2$ ............(ii)

$- 2x - y = 3$ ........(iii)

On solving equation (i), (ii) and (iii) we get,

$x = \frac{ - 1}{6},y = \frac{ - 8}{3},z = \frac{3}{2}$

So, $3\vec{c}.\vec{a} = 29$

questions.explanation:
A plane containing two vectors can be expressed as a linear combination of the vectors.

Hence, let $\vec{x} = \lambda \vec{a} + \mu \vec{b}(\lambda$ and $\mu$ are scalars$). \implies \vec{x} = \hat{i}(2\lambda + \mu ) + \hat{j}(2\mu - \lambda ) + \hat{k}(\lambda - \mu )$

Since $\vec{x}$ is perpendicular to $3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}, \implies \vec{x} \cdot \left(3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}\right) = 0 \implies \left(\hat{i}(2\lambda + \mu ) + \hat{j}(2\mu - \lambda ) + \hat{k}(\lambda - \mu )\right) \cdot \left(3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}\right) = 0 \implies 3(2\lambda + \mu ) + 2(2\mu - \lambda ) - (\lambda - \mu ) = 0 \implies 3\lambda + 8\mu = 0...\left(1\right)$

Also, the projection of $\vec{x}$ on $\vec{a}$ is $\frac{17\sqrt{6}}{2} \implies \frac{\vec{x} \cdot \vec{a}}{ | \vec{a} | } = \frac{17\sqrt{6}}{2} \implies \frac{\left(\hat{i}(2\lambda + \mu ) + \hat{j}(2\mu - \lambda ) + \hat{k}(\lambda - \mu )\right) \cdot \left(2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}\right)}{\sqrt{{2}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}} = \frac{17\sqrt{6}}{2} \implies \frac{2(2\lambda + \mu ) - (2\mu - \lambda ) + (\lambda - \mu )}{\sqrt{6}} = \frac{17\sqrt{6}}{2} \implies 6\lambda - \mu = 51...\left(2\right)$

On solving the equations $(1)$ and $(2),$ we get $\lambda = 8,\mu = - 3.$

Thus, $\vec{x} = 13\hat{i} - 14\hat{j} + 11\hat{k} \implies \left(\vec{x}\right) = \sqrt{{13}^{2} + {\left( - 14\right)}^{2} + {11}^{2}} \implies | \vec{x}{ | }^{2} = 486.$

$\vec{c}=\left(\frac{\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}}{|\vec{b}|}\right) \frac{\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|} \begin{aligned} & \quad=\left(\frac{\lambda+8}{9}\right)(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}) \\ & |\vec{a}+\vec{c}|=7 \\ & \left.\Rightarrow\left(\frac{\lambda+8}{9}+1\right) \hat{i}+\left(\frac{2(\lambda+8)}{9}+2\right) \hat{j}+\left(\frac{2(\lambda+8)}{9}+2\right) \hat{k} \right\rvert\,=7 \\ & \left(\frac{\lambda+8}{9}+1\right)^2+\left(\frac{2(\lambda+8)}{9}+2\right)^2+\left(\frac{2(\lambda+8)}{9}+2\right)^2=49\end{aligned} \Rightarrow \lambda=4 \Rightarrow \vec{c}=\frac{4}{3} \hat{i}+\frac{8}{3} \hat{j}+\frac{8}{3} \hat{k}$
Area of parallelogram $=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \frac{4}{3} & \frac{8}{3} & \frac{8}{3} \\ 4 & 0 & 4\end{array}\right|=16$

questions.question:
Let $a$ and $b$ be two unit vectors such that $\left(\left(a + b\right) + 2\left(a \times b\right)\right) = 2$. If $\theta \in \left(0,\pi \right)$ is the angle between $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$, then among the statements:

$\left(S1\right) : 2\left(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}\right) = \left(\hat{a} - \hat{b}\right) \left(S2\right)$ : The projection of $\hat{a}$ on $\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right)$ is $\frac{1}{2}$
questions.explanation:
Given,

$\left(\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right) + 2\left(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}\right)\right) = 2,\theta \in \left(0,\pi \right)$

Squaring both side we get,

$\left(\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right) + 2\left(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}\right)\right) \cdot \left(\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right) + 2\left(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}\right)\right) = 4 {\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right)}^{2} + 4{\left(\left(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}\right)\right)}^{2} + 0 = 4$

Let the angle be $\theta$ between $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b} \implies {\left(\hat{a}\right)}^{2} + {\left(\hat{b}\right)}^{2} + 2\left(\hat{a}\right)\left(\hat{b}\right)\cos \theta + 4\left(\left(\hat{a}\right)\left(\hat{b}\right)\sin \theta \right) = 4 \implies 2 + 2\cos \theta + 4{\sin }^{2}\theta = 4 \implies 2 + 2\cos \theta - 4{\cos }^{2}\theta = 0$

Let $\cos \theta = t$ then

$\implies 2{t}^{2} - t - 1 = 0 \implies 2{t}^{2} - 2t + t - 1 = 0 \implies 2t\left(t - 1\right) + \left(t - 1\right) = 0 \left(2t + 1\right)\left(t - 1\right) = 0$

So, $t = - \frac{1}{2}$ or $t = 1$

Then, $\cos \theta = - \frac{1}{2}$ or $\cos \theta = 1$ which is not possible as $0 \in \left(0,\pi \right)$

So, $\theta = \frac{2\pi }{3}$

Now,

${S}_{1} \implies 2\left(a \times b\right) = 2\sin \left(\frac{2\pi }{3}\right) = 2 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \sqrt{3}$

And $\left(\hat{a} - \hat{b}\right) = \sqrt{1 + 1 - 2\cos \left(\frac{2\pi }{3}\right)} = \sqrt{2 - 2 \times \left( - \frac{1}{2}\right)} = \sqrt{3} {S}_{1}$ is correct.

${S}_{2}$ projection of $\hat{a}$ on $\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right) \implies \frac{\hat{a}.\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right)}{∣\hat{a} + \hat{b})} = \frac{1 + \cos \left(\frac{2\pi }{3}\right)}{\sqrt{2 + 2\cos \frac{2\pi }{3}}} \implies \frac{1 - \frac{1}{2}}{\sqrt{1}} = \frac{1}{2}$

Which is true, So both are true.

questions.explanation:
Let $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$ be two unit vectors such that the angle between them is $\frac{\pi }{4}$. If $\theta$ is the angle between the vectors $\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right)$ and $\left(\hat{a} + 2\hat{b} + 2\left(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}\right)\right)$ then the value of $164{\cos }^{2}\theta$ is equal to

Now let angle between $\hat{a} & \hat{b} = \frac{\pi }{4} = ϕ$

So, $\hat{a} \cdot \hat{b} = \left(\hat{a}\right)\left(\hat{b}\right)\cos ϕ \implies \hat{a} \cdot \hat{b} = \cos ϕ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Now finding angle between $\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right) & \left(\hat{a} + 2\hat{b} + 2\left(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}\right)\right)$ we get,

$\cos \theta = \frac{\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right) \cdot \left(\hat{a} + 2\hat{b} + 2\left(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}\right)\right)}{\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right)\left(\hat{a} + 2\hat{b} + 2\left(\hat{a} \times \hat{b}\right)\right)}....\left(1\right)$

Now finding the value of ${\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right)}^{2} = \left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right) \cdot \left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right) \implies {\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right)}^{2} = 2 + 2\hat{a} \cdot \hat{b} = 2 + \sqrt{2}$

Also value of $\hat{a} \times \hat{b} = \left(\hat{a}\right)\left(\hat{b}\right)\sin ϕ\hat{n} \implies \hat{a} \times \hat{b} = \frac{\hat{n}}{\sqrt{2}}$ when $\hat{n}$ is vector $⊥$to $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$

Let $\vec{c} = \hat{a} \times \hat{b}$

We know that, $\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} = 0$ and $\vec{c} \cdot \vec{b} = 0$ as perpendicular vector dot product is zero.

Now value of ${\left(\hat{a} + 2\hat{b} + 2\vec{c}\right)}^{2} = 1 + 4 + \frac{\left(4\right)}{2} + 4\hat{a} \cdot \hat{b} + 8\hat{b} \cdot \vec{c} + 4\vec{c} \cdot \hat{a} = 7 + \frac{4}{\sqrt{2}} = 7 + 2\sqrt{2}$

Now finding dot product we get, $\left(\hat{a} + \hat{b}\right) \cdot \left(\hat{a} + 2\hat{b} + 2\vec{c}\right) = {\left(\hat{a}\right)}^{2} + 2\hat{a} \cdot \hat{b} + 0 + \hat{b} \cdot \hat{a} + 2{\left(\hat{b}\right)}^{2} + 0 = 1 + \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 2 = 3 + \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}$

Now putting all the values in equation $\left(1\right)$ we get,

$\cos \theta = \frac{3 + \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}}{\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2}}\sqrt{7 + 2\sqrt{2}}} \implies {\cos }^{2}\theta = \frac{9{\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}^{2}}{2\left(2 + \sqrt{2}\right)\left(7 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)} \implies {\cos }^{2}\theta = \left(\frac{9}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)\frac{\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}{\left(7 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)} \implies 164{\cos }^{2}\theta = \frac{\left(82\right)\left(9\right)}{\sqrt{2}}\frac{\left(\sqrt{2} + 1\right)}{\left(7 + 2\sqrt{2}\right)}\frac{\left(7 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)}{\left(7 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)} \implies 164{\cos }^{2}\theta = \frac{\left(82\right)}{\sqrt{2}}\frac{\left(9\right)\left(7\sqrt{2} - 4 + 7 - 2\sqrt{2}\right)}{\left(41\right)} \implies 164{\cos }^{2}\theta = \left(9\sqrt{2}\right)\left(5\sqrt{2} + 3\right) \implies 164{\cos }^{2}\theta = 90 + 27\sqrt{2}$

Then the value of $\left(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\right)$ is equal to
questions.explanation:
Given, $\left(\vec{a}\right) = 9$

And $\left(x\vec{a} + y\vec{b}\right) \cdot \left(6y\vec{a} - 18x\vec{b}\right) = 0 \left(\text{as they are perpendicular}\right) \implies 6xy{\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2} - 18{x}^{2}\left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}\right) + 6{y}^{2}\left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}\right) - 18xy{\left(\vec{b}\right)}^{2} = 0 \implies 6xy\left({\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2} - 3{\left(\vec{b}\right)}^{2}\right) + \left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}\right)\left({y}^{2} - 3{x}^{2}\right) = 0$

This should hold $∀x,y \in R \times R - \left(\left(0,0\right)\right)$

So, ${\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2} - 3{\left(\vec{b}\right)}^{2} = 0 & \left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}\right) = 0 ∴{\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2} = 3{\left(\vec{b}\right)}^{2} & \left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}\right) = 0 \implies \cos \theta = 0 \implies \theta = 90 ^\circ$

Now ${\left(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\right)}^{2} = {\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2}{\left(\vec{b}\right)}^{2}{\sin }^{2}\theta = {\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2}{\left(\vec{b}\right)}^{2}\left(\text{as }\theta = {90}^{ ^\circ }\right) = {\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2} \cdot \frac{{\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2}}{3} \left(\text{as }{\left(\vec{b}\right)}^{2} = \frac{{\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2}}{3}\right)$

So, $\left(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\right) = \frac{{\left(\vec{a}\right)}^{2}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{81}{\sqrt{3}} = 27\sqrt{3}$

Let

$\vec{b} = x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}$

Then,

$\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \left( \begin{matrix}\hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ - 1 & - 1 & 1 \\ x & y & z\end{matrix} \right) \implies \vec{a} \times \vec{b} = - \left(y + z\right)\hat{i} + \left(x + z\right)\hat{j} + \left(x - y\right)\hat{k}$

So,

$- \left(y + z\right)\hat{i} + \left(x + z\right)\hat{j} + \left(x - y\right)\hat{k} = \hat{i} - \hat{j} + 0\hat{k}$

$y + z = - 1\;$

$\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 1 \implies - x - y + z = 1 \implies - 2x + z = 1 \implies z = 2x + 1 \implies - 1 - x = 2x + 1 \implies 3x = - 2 \implies x = - \frac{2}{3}$

So, $y = - \frac{2}{3};z = - \frac{1}{3}$

Hence,

$\vec{b} = - \frac{2}{3}\hat{i} - \frac{2}{3}\hat{j} - \frac{1}{3}\hat{k} \implies 6\vec{b} = - 4\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$

So,

$\vec{a} - 6\vec{b} = 3\left(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}\right)$

questions.explanation: We have, ${\vec{v}}_{1} = \sqrt{3}p\hat{i} + \hat{j} {\vec{v}}_{2} = 2\hat{i} + \left(p + 1\right)\hat{j} \tan \theta = \frac{\left(\alpha \sqrt{3} - 2\right)}{\left(4\sqrt{3} + 3\right)}$ $\left({\vec{v}}_{1}\right) = \left({\vec{v}}_{2}\right) \implies 3{p}^{2} + 1 = 4 + (p + 1{)}^{2} \implies 2{p}^{2} - 2p - 4 = 0 \implies {p}^{2} - p - 2 = 0 \implies p = 2, - 1$ (rejected) Now, $\cos \theta = \frac{{\vec{v}}_{1} \cdot {\vec{v}}_{2}}{\left({\vec{v}}_{1}\right) \cdot \left({\vec{v}}_{2}\right)} = \frac{2\sqrt{3}p + (p + 1)}{\sqrt{(p + 1{)}^{2} + 4}\sqrt{3{p}^{2} + 1}} \implies \cos \theta = \frac{4\sqrt{3} + 3}{\sqrt{13}\sqrt{13}} = \frac{4\sqrt{3} + 3}{13} \implies \tan \theta = \frac{\sqrt{112 - 24\sqrt{3}}}{4\sqrt{3} + 3} = \frac{\sqrt{{\left(6\sqrt{3} - 2\right)}^{2}}}{4\sqrt{3} + 3} \implies \tan \theta = \frac{6\sqrt{3} - 2}{4\sqrt{3} + 3} = \frac{\alpha \sqrt{3} - 2}{4\sqrt{3} + 3} \implies \alpha = 6$

questions.question: Let $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k},\vec{b} = −\hat{i}−8\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c} = 4\hat{i} + {c}_{2}\hat{j} + {c}_{3}\hat{k}$ be three vectors such that $\vec{b} \times \vec{a} = \vec{c} \times \vec{a}$. If the angle between the vector $\vec{c}$ and the vector $3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ is $\theta$, then the greatest integer less than or equal to ${\tan }^{2}\theta$ is:
questions.explanation:
Given: $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + k$, $\vec{b} = −\hat{i}−8\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c} = 4\hat{i} + {c}_{2}\hat{j} + {c}_{3}k$

Also, $\vec{b} \times \vec{a} = \vec{c} \times \vec{a} \implies \left(\vec{b}−\vec{c}\right) \times \vec{a} = 0 \implies \vec{b}−\vec{c} = \lambda \vec{a} \implies \vec{b} = \vec{c} + \lambda \vec{a} \implies −\hat{i} - 8\hat{j} + 2k = \left(4\hat{i} + {c}_{2}\hat{j} + {c}_{3}k\right) + \lambda \left(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + k\right) \implies \lambda + 4 = −1,\lambda + {c}_{2} = −8,\lambda + {c}_{3} = 2 \implies \lambda = −5,{c}_{2} = −3,{c}_{3} = 7 \implies \vec{c} = 4\hat{i}−3\hat{j} + 7k$

Now, finding angle we get,

$\cos \theta = \frac{\left(3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + \hat{k}\right) \cdot \left(4\hat{i}−3\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}\right)}{\left(\left(3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + \hat{k}\right)\right)⋅\left(\left(4\hat{i}−3\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}\right)\right)} \implies \cos \theta = \frac{12−12 + 7}{\sqrt{26}⋅\sqrt{74}} \implies \cos \theta = \frac{7}{\sqrt{26}⋅\sqrt{74}} \implies \cos \theta = \frac{7}{2\sqrt{481}} \implies \sec \theta = \frac{2\sqrt{481}}{7} \implies {\sec }^{2}\theta = \frac{4 \times 481}{49} \implies 1 + {\tan }^{2}\theta = \frac{1924}{49} \implies {\tan }^{2}\theta = \frac{1875}{49} \implies {\tan }^{2}\theta \approx 38.26 \implies \left({\tan }^{2}\theta \right) = \left(38.26\right) = 38$
